title: Red eyes over the TNT area
story: Driving past the old igloos just after ten. Two red lights rose above the treeline and crossed the road without a sound — no engine, no flapping. My headlights caught a shape like a man with wings folded. It matched every Mothman description I had ever read: red reflective eyes, huge wingspan, silent flight. I sat in the car for five minutes before I could drive on.

title: Something tall crossed Route 33
story: Tall figure, maybe seven feet, stepped out of the corn and crossed Route 33 in three strides. I only saw it from the side and it was raining hard. Could have been a person in a coat. Mentioning the red eyes because my passenger swears they saw a red glint, but I did not see that myself.

title: Pants walking on my lawn at 2am
story: Doorbell cam caught a white figure with long legs and no arms gliding across the lawn. No head visible in the frame, just legs that kept going. Walked exactly like the famous Fresno footage — gliding walk, no arms, about four feet tall. Uploaded the clip; the timestamp and the neighbor's porch light match.

title: White legs by the canal
story: Saw pale legs moving along the canal bank from about a hundred yards. No torso visible over the embankment. Honestly it could have been a heron in bad light, but the stride looked wrong for a bird and I have watched herons here for years.

title: Three goats down, no blood
story: Found three goats dead at dawn, each with two small punctures at the throat and almost no blood at the scene. No tracks I could identify — the ground was too hard. The livestock drained of blood pattern matches the chupacabra reports from the nineties exactly, and nothing else out here hunts like that.

title: Mangy dog, probably just a dog
story: Mangy gray canid with patchy fur sniffing around the deer feeder. No spines, no quills, did not touch any livestock. Filing this because the app asked for honesty: this was almost certainly a coyote with mange, and I want the record to show the workflow can say no.

title: Scream in the Barrens
story: Camped off Batsto Road. At half past eleven something screamed — not a fox, not an owl, a long descending wail that set both dogs off. Next morning I found cloven-looking prints in the mud by the creek, too big for deer and in a straight line like something hopping. The unearthly scream and the prints together are why I am filing this as Jersey Devil rather than wildlife.

title: Hoofprints after snowfall
story: Single line of hoofprints across fresh snow behind the shed, starting and stopping in the middle of the yard. Classic Leeds-devil lore. No photos worth anything — melted by noon — so judge this one on the description alone.

title: Long wake off South Bass
story: Flat calm evening. A wake thirty feet long moved against the wind with three humps showing, then a head like a dog on a long neck came up twice. Two other boaters saw it. No photo — by the time anyone grabbed a phone it was gone. Late-summer appearance fits Bessie's pattern to the week.

title: Knocks answered back
story: Knocked twice on a dead cedar. Ten seconds later two knocks came back from the drainage, same rhythm, deeper timber. Then a smell like wet dog and rot rolled through camp and something big moved off breaking branches at knee height or higher. Wood knocks plus the odor plus movement — the full Bluff Creek bingo card.

title: Trail-cam blur, inconclusive
story: Trail cam caught a dark upright blur for two frames. Could be a bear standing up. Could be a hiker in a ghillie suit. Filing it because the timestamp and location are solid, but I am voting reject on my own report — this is exactly the kind of blur the workflow should refuse to publish.

title: Jackalope at the taxidermist
story: It is a stuffed rabbit with horns on the wall of a shop that sells postcards admitting it is fake. Verifying this would prove the pipeline publishes anything, so this report exists to be rejected.
